articles.title: How to Choose the Right One for Your CI/CD Pipeline
articles.excerpt: AI API Testing Tools: How to Choose the Right One for Your CI/CD Pipeline AI is making it easier to generate test cases, but there is a problem: generating more tests does not necessarily mean finding…
articles.body: AI API Testing Tools: How to Choose the Right One for Your CI/CD Pipeline AI is making it easier to generate test cases, but there is a problem: generating more tests does not necessarily mean finding more bugs. Some tools generate tests from API specifications. Others record real HTTP traffic, help developers write assertions, or use AI to maintain existing tests. Although these tools are often grouped under the label “AI testing,” they solve different engineering problems. If you are evaluating AI-powered API testing tools for your development team, the first step is to understand what you want to automate. In this article, we will look at the main approaches, how to evaluate them, and what to consider before integrating generated tests into a CI/CD pipeline. 1.

articles.title: Your habit did not die from doing too little. It died from day four.
articles.excerpt: You did not quit your habit because you were lazy. You quit because of day four, when the thing you had built so carefully had quietly turned into a 30-minute obligation and you could not find 30 minu…
articles.body: You did not quit your habit because you were lazy. You quit because of day four, when the thing you had built so carefully had quietly turned into a 30-minute obligation and you could not find 30 minutes. That is the part almost nobody talks about. The failure is not at the start. It is at the moment the habit gets bigger than the reason you started . What usually happens in week one Day 1 is easy. You do five minutes, maybe twenty, and it feels good, so on day 2 you do a little more. By day 5 the thing has a shape, and the shape is "this takes half an hour". Day 8 you are tired, the half hour is not there, and you skip it. Day 9 you skip it again because day 8 already happened. The habit did not die from doing too little. It died from the size you grew it to in the first week.

articles.title: Open Source Code Review Tools for GitHub and Self-Hosted Teams
articles.excerpt: Open source code review tools fall into two groups, and search results often mix them. Open source code review tools for GitHub run inside pull requests you already have: a GitHub Action or a CLI post…
articles.body: Open source code review tools fall into two groups, and search results often mix them. Open source code review tools for GitHub run inside pull requests you already have: a GitHub Action or a CLI posts on the pull request, and the repository stays on GitHub. Self-hosted Git forges and review servers are the other group: they are where the repository, or the review request, lives. MergeJudge (mergejudge.si) is an AI pull request reviewer with an open-source engine for GitHub. The engine, the Action and the runner CLI are MIT-licensed in gauravsharmaGG/mergejudge-runner . Every pull request is sorted into an auto , review or block lane. Deterministic rules set the floor, and the AI step can only raise that lane. auto means low risk, not a guarantee.

articles.title: The 'or' that read too far
articles.excerpt: Verbose is a small language I build that compiles to native x86-64, to WebAssembly, and also runs in an interpreter. This post walks through one bug that showed up differently in each of those, with r…
articles.body: Verbose is a small language I build that compiles to native x86-64, to WebAssembly, and also runs in an interpreter. This post walks through one bug that showed up differently in each of those, with real binaries. It stands on its own; no Verbose knowledge needed. Before reading the first line of a notebook, you check there is something in it. Nobody does it the other way round. Nobody opens an empty notebook, tries to read line one, and then thinks "ah, it was empty, never mind". In Verbose, that precaution is written like this: length(i.s) == 0 or byte_at(i.s, 0) > 0 "The text is empty, or its first byte is nonzero." If the text is empty, the question is settled by the first half, and the second half, which reads byte number zero, has no reason to be asked.

articles.excerpt: I've been quietly building Antigravity Tools — a collection of 59 free, browser-based developer utilities — and today I'm sharing everything I built and learned. The main constraint I set for myself:…
articles.body: I've been quietly building Antigravity Tools — a collection of 59 free, browser-based developer utilities — and today I'm sharing everything I built and learned. Why vanilla JS? No React, no build step. The main constraint I set for myself: zero dependencies, zero server, zero telemetry . When you paste your JWT token into jwt.io, it goes to their server. When you use an online regex tester, your test strings are logged. I built Antigravity Tools so every operation runs inside your browser, using native APIs. No Node.js backend No npm packages No webpack/vite/parcel No Google Analytics No cookies Everything runs on Web Crypto API , Canvas API , Web Audio API , and IndexedDB — all native to modern browsers.

articles.title: Exploring Open-Source Large Language Models for InkMind: Choosing a Better Poetry Continuation Model
articles.excerpt: Exploring Open-Source Large Language Models for InkMind: Choosing a Better Poetry Continuation Model Introduction Large Language Models (LLMs) have become important tools in natural language processin…
articles.body: Exploring Open-Source Large Language Models for InkMind: Choosing a Better Poetry Continuation Model Introduction Large Language Models (LLMs) have become important tools in natural language processing (NLP). They can generate text, summarize information, answer questions, and assist with creative writing. Most modern text-generating LLMs use the Transformer architecture and learn patterns in language from large collections of text. Our project, InkMind , focuses on poetry generation through text continuation. Unlike an instruction-based chatbot, InkMind receives an opening phrase or part of a poem and generates the following words. For example, given the input “Beneath the moon, I walk alone,” the model should continue the text in a coherent and creative way.

articles.excerpt: Counting the Boxes: A 2,185-Asset Inventory of BeyondTrust Remote Support Edge Appliances Edge appliances are reachable from the internet by design. When a zero-day lands on one of them, the question…
articles.body: Counting the Boxes: A 2,185-Asset Inventory of BeyondTrust Remote Support Edge Appliances Edge appliances are reachable from the internet by design. When a zero-day lands on one of them, the question stops being theoretical and becomes an inventory question. CVE-2026-102764 is a case in point. What the public record establishes BeyondTrust published advisory BT26-05 for its Remote Support product, and the National Vulnerability Database describes the flaw as inadequate validation of the origin of messages handled by internal components, allowing an attacker to perform file operations on the appliance. NVD maps it to CWE-290, authentication bypass by spoofing, and scores it CVSS 4.0 9.3 and CVSS 3.1 9.8, both with network attack vector, no privileges required and no user interaction.

articles.excerpt: Multiple user profiles could soon be able to view and manage their data using Health Connect, all from one device.
articles.body: TL;DR A future Android update may finally let multiple user profiles access Health Connect. Health Connect currently supports only one user, but code in the recent Android 17 QPR3 Beta 2 suggests that could change. If implemented, this would let multiple users manage app permissions and view or delete their existing health data, all from one device. Google Health Connect is a built-in Android tool that lets supported fitness and health apps read, write, and share data, while keeping it secure and on-device. Due to current limitations, Health Connect doesn’t support multiple user profiles, meaning its features aren’t available on other profiles. Thankfully, a future Android release could change that. articles.title: Rubin telescope should find more of Earth's mysterious 'mini-moons' — including some we can study up close
articles.excerpt: Earth’s tiny, temporary moons could become some of the easiest asteroid targets for future missions. And we'll likely find more of them soon, thanks to the Rubin telescope.
articles.body: Earth almost always has more than one moon. The others are just very small, and they never stay long — but they could provide accessible and unique insights into the solar system. Temporary satellites, or mini-moons , are small asteroids that wander into Earth’s neighborhood and get captured briefly by our planet’s gravity. A typical one stays about nine months and circles Earth roughly three times before escaping back into orbit around the sun , Grigori Fedorets of Finland's University of Helsinki said in a presentation at the Europlanet Science Congress (EPSC) 2026 in The Hague in September. Fedorets' modeling suggests that the largest mini-moon around Earth at any given moment is typically only about 75 centimeters (30 inches) across.

articles.title: 'More missions, more often': NASA is overhauling how it selects science missions
articles.excerpt: NASA is overhauling how it selects and develops science missions, with changes intended to reduce costs, streamline competition and get missions into space faster.
articles.body: NASA is overhauling how it selects and develops science missions, with changes intended to reduce costs, streamline competition and get missions into space faster. The new approach, called Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), was announced on Oct. 21 in an open letter from Nicky Fox, associate administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate (SMD), to the NASA science community. The changes, directed by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, could significantly reshape how scientists, universities, NASA centers and commercial companies vie for future missions. "We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long," Fox stated in the letter.
